column2: He felt he was not yet ready to face what to do with the country, or whether he could lead so many people. So he made up his mind and yielded the throne to another powerful noble.

Even after becoming a noble, he lived mostly among the common folk. He felt it suited him. And even in old age he kept listening to the voices of the people and striving to reflect them in government,
believing that it is ordinary people who hold up a country...
Rocus Las Flores: struggling against the lot he had been given, he came to realise on his journey what he truly ought to do.
Thinking again about what he could do, he decided this time to travel the world of his own free will. He resolved to save as many common people as he could with his own hands.

The new journey became a harsh trial for him. Misfortunes like poverty and famine that no one person could fix, epidemics that even his hands could not cure; at times he even despaired at his own powerlessness.
But he kept believing that what he could do, even the small things he was doing now, would one day become a force to change the future, and he travelled on in silence.

Time passed, and in the prime of life he returned to the Holy City upon the death of the Vice Pope. Many people begged him to, but he also thought that now, as Pope, he might be able to do something new. Having become the new Pope, he reformed the Church and made it once more a church for the people.
The future he believed in is, even after he is gone, slowly coming true through the Church.
Rocus's journey of training seems to be going on still.
Through the journey to save the world, he must have learned what he can do with his own power, and where the people he should help are.
This time by his own wish, he has left the rebuilt Church behind and is reaching out to people all over the world, never minding if his robes get dirty...

No one knows why the power of the healing hands was given to him. But now that he no longer resents that power, one day he will surely understand its meaning: how precious it is to live for someone else...
Rocus Las Flores, who had struggled on and on to escape his fate, finished his journey and returned to the Holy Nation.
The Vice Pope acknowledged his change of heart, and he was at last set to take the Pope's seat. But the Church, unable to cut its age-old ties, brought him pain.
Aiming at great reforms, Rocus met with setback after setback. Each time he thought of resigning as Pope, but the Vice Pope held him back.
Thanks to his patient efforts, the Church is slowly becoming a church for the people...
Long time no see, Raviel.
You again? What is it this time?
Oh, it's you... Something to discuss?
What, again? Is it urgent?
What is it... So early in the morning...
Hey, Raviel.
It's been a long time.
What's the matter?
What is it? At this late hour.
What is it, so early in the morning?
Do you need something, Angel?
What? Again, so soon? Did something happen?
